title: SLO-cost-tradeoff-pitch-examples-for-eng-roles
content:
Purpose / where to use this:
Quick reference playbook with concrete talk tracks for initial discovery through procurement, framed as an SLO vs cost conversation. Designed to help AE/SE/GTM SMEs run technically credible calls with ML engineers, backend engineers, and platform teams — without getting stuck in abstract feature bingo.

High level framing (1-liner for each persona):
- ML engineers: “We help you meet model quality SLOs at predictable token cost while preserving experimentability (version pinning + eval hooks).”
- Backend engineers: “We let you serve predictable latency and throughput SLOs for LLM endpoints with observability and graceful fallback so app SLAs don’t break.”
- Platform teams: “We provide a unified runtime and deployment abstraction so you can standardize inference across hosted, dedicated, and private environments with capacity controls and auditability.”

Quick openers (30s):
- For MLEs: “Hey — when you evaluate models, do you worry more about subtle regressions after quantization or raw serving throughput? We run small eval suites tied to deployments so you get early regression alerts and concrete cost delta estimates.”
- For Backend: “If your app p95 jumps during peak, do you have a fallback that preserves user experience? Redwood routes to compatible model variants and has per-route latency-based fallback policies.”
- For Platform: “How do you map budgeted GPU commit to SLOs across teams? Redwood Dedicated lets you carve predictable pools and autoscale within budget with clear headroom policies.”

Two-minute technical talk (tailored by persona):
- MLE (focus: fidelity + experiments):
  - Show: model catalog + version pinning + eval-triggers on rollout.
  - Explain: how prefix/KV caching + selective quantization profiles retain quality while dropping per-token cost.
  - Demo ask: run one eval of a noisy prompt set, compare baseline vs int8/awq, show metric deltas and suggested rollback threshold.

- Backend (focus: latency + throughput):
  - Show: request pipeline (smart routing, batching, KV cache), p50/p95 telemetry, and fallbacks.
  - Explain: batching policy tradeoffs (latency vs throughput) with concrete numbers from similar customers (e.g., 20% cost reduction at 1.4x p95 with adaptive batching).
  - Demo ask: a short perf run with 100 concurrent synthetic users to show p95 under load and an automated fallback flip.

- Platform (focus: ops + compliance):
  - Show: Dedicated capacity UI, VPC topology, audit logs, KMS integration.
  - Explain: commit sizing logic (how committed GPUs map to expected qps for typical sequence lengths).
  - Demo ask: a quick mapping exercise: take their peak QPS and typical seq length, produce a 30-day cost projection with burst headroom.

Concrete SLO vs cost tradeoff scripts (copy/paste friendly):
- Discovery Bumpers (MLE):
  - "Goal: validate model fidelity in production. If we quantify the delta from 16-bit to our quantized profile and it's < 1% on your eval metric, you save ~30–45% token cost. Would a 1% threshold be acceptable?"
- Discovery Bumpers (Backend):
  - "Goal: p95 under 300ms. We can reach this by pinning a lower-latency variant for hot routes and routing long-tail requests to cheaper models. Which routes can tolerate higher latency?"
- Discovery Bumpers (Platform):
  - "Goal: 99.9% uptime for inference and predictable monthly bill. We map commit to SLOs — how many teams and peak QPS are we sizing for?"

Objection handling (short):
- "We already have on-prem infra" -> "Great, Redwood Private provides the same runtime and rollout tools behind your VPC so your execs keep control while devs use the same API and telemetry."
- "Quantization breaks quality" -> "We run your eval suite on quantized variants and tie rollouts to metric-based gates; we can show your actual metric delta before you commit."
- "Costs look unpredictable" -> "We propose a short performance benchmark (7 days synthetic + traffic replay) and then a recommended batching/cache profile that converts observed traffic into a predictable cost-per-1M tokens number."

Competitor notes (short signals to mention/avoid):
- General cloud AI endpoints (GCP/Azure/AWS): strong for generality but weaker on inference-ops automation (e.g., KV cache, model variant routing) and customer-configurable rollout policies. Avoid positioning as purely “cheaper” — emphasize operational controls and developer DX.
- LLM API pure plays: good UX, inconsistent SLAs for high-throughput apps. Call out the gap around enterprise-dedicated capacity + private control plane.
- Inference infra vendors/self-hosted runtimes: good flexibility but heavier ops burden. Emphasize Redwood’s hybrid: same runtime, managed plugin points, and optional private control plane.

Positioning bullets (elevator to technical exec):
- Unified runtime: one API across hosted, dedicated, private. Means fewer integrations and fewer support incidents.
- SLO-first economics: we start with the SLO you need and show the concrete combo of model variant, batching, caching that meets it at the lowest projected cost.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency, per-route/traces, and eval hooks so regressions are visible before rollouts.
- Graceful degradation: automatic fallback chains (model variant -> region -> capacity tier) to keep app surface available.

Evaluation/trial checklist (what the SE asks for):
- Traffic profile: peak QPS, typical seq length distribution, token mix (system/user), % streaming.
- Success metrics: p50/p95 latency, throughput, acceptable quality delta (top metric), cost per 1M tokens target.
- Datasets: small eval set (200–1000 examples) that represents critical edge cases.
- Access: sample queries, sample payload sizes, and basic identity for private connections if needed.
- Timeline: 7–14 day perf + quality run, results review, then 30-day pilot with real traffic routing.

Playbook examples (short A/B scripts to run with teams):
- 1) MLE: Eval-first path
  - Day 0–2: ingest eval set, baseline run (fp16), quantized run (candidate). Report delta and suggested quant profile.
  - Day 3–7: small canary in hosted or private test cluster, collect traffic-sim metrics.
  - Acceptance: <1% metric delta AND cost gain >30%.

- 2) Backend: Latency-first path
  - Day 0–3: traffic replay for p95 target, tune batching and cache TTLs.
  - Day 4–10: run full concurrency test with fallback on to ensure SLA in region outage simulation.
  - Acceptance: p95 under agreed SLA in 95% of windows and automated fallback validated.

- 3) Platform: Commit-sizing path
  - Day 0: capture peak and avg QPS + seq length hist.
  - Day 1–5: sizing calc -> propose commit GPU pool and autoscale bands.
  - Acceptance: projected spend within 10% of target and headroom policy approved.

Example email to MLE after call (short):
Hi <name>,
Thanks for the call — attaching the quick eval plan we discussed. If you can drop a 300–500 example eval set and give us a baseline run on your metric, we’ll return quantization deltas + suggested rollout gates by EOD Day 3. If that looks good we’ll spin a small canary in your test cluster.
Regards,
Samira

Notes to self / TODOs: (very informal)
- Add ballpark numbers from recent case studies (need approvals from case study owners).
- Build one-pager comparing 3 common fallback policies with cost delta examples.
- Validate the phrasing around "quantization preserves fidelity" with research team — don't overclaim.
- Confirm recommended default thresholds: 1% metric delta for MLEs, 300ms p95 for mid-market backends.

Why this doc is different from other GTM persona artifacts:
- Focused on a single conversational axis (SLO vs cost) rather than persona framing only.
- Provides concrete asks, trial steps, and copy/paste scripts for AE/SE to use in live calls.
- Mix of technical specifics (batching, KV cache, quant profiles) and contractual sizing (commit mapping to GPU pools) so it helps across discovery -> procurement.

Appendix: quick jargon cheat sheet (for non-technical stakeholders on call)
- KV cache: per-session key-value cache for decoder states — saves tokens for repeated context.
- Quant profiles: quantization config (e.g., int8/awq) tuned per model to trade precision vs throughput.
- Model variant: a compatible model variant tuned for latency/cost that preserves critical behavior for the route.

End.
